use_case_summary: Realtime chat for driver support: strict interactive latency requirements (operational agents on mobile devices).
Reranking for search & routing decisions: throughput-heavy batch workloads during peak hours (evening surge).
Summarization for tickets: lower latency sensitivity but high QPS for nightly backfills.
latency_slo_requirements: Target SLOs proposed by customer: p50 <= 60ms (token-level for streaming), p95 <= 250ms (end-to-end), p99 <= 700ms (end-to-end) for non-streaming short prompts
Streaming vs non-streaming: prefer separate SLO buckets. Streaming clients measure first-byte and incremental tokens; non-streaming measure full-response completion.
Throughput expectations: baseline sustained 600 concurrent streaming sessions; burst to 2k for 15 minutes with reserved GPUs scaled accordingly.
Reserved GPU planning: initial commit = 8xA100-equiv for dedicated pool; ask for sizing guidance for steady-state vs burst capacity and autoscaling buffer.
measurement_alignment: Agreement to align on client-side timing (timestamp at request send) and server-side timing (ingest -> first-token -> final-token) with translation rules between them.
Definition doc will include: metric names, aggregation windows, clock sync guidance (NTP/clock skew tolerance), and instrumentation libs for mobile/web clients.
We'll capture both 'first-byte latency' (streaming first-token) and 'tail completion latency' (non-streaming final-token).
Plan: synthetic load tests for baseline + 2-week shadowing of production traffic (non-invasive) to capture real-user latencies and error modes.
Important: clarify how model truncation, tokenization variance, and KV cache hits change latency distributions; record tokens-per-response as dimension.
sla_expectations: SLA wanted: 99.9% uptime for dedicated capacity; latency targets as above with credits for missed monthly SLOs; formalized in term sheet.
